_note: Month-specific copy. Strings are Jinja templates rendered against the market data file, so numbers are pulled from data rather than typed. Review every sentence when the data changes — the judgments (e.g. 'buyer-leaning') are not automatic. September 2026 changes from August: single-family median went NEGATIVE (-1.3%) and days to contract ROSE (44 to 52), so the August 'tilting to sellers' verdict and every 'contract time fell' sentence were rewritten. Condo volume in this county is small — 91 closings — so the +24.1% median is deliberately never framed as a change in condo values.
glanceLede: Inventory is down from a year ago in both property types, but single-family homes and condos/townhomes are otherwise sending different signals. Here are the four key measures for each, side by side.

verdicts.label: Single-family homes
verdicts.note: Supply eased from {{ s.sfh.m.monthsSupply.prior | dec1 }} months; sales closed at {{ s.sfh.m.olpReceived.current | dec1 }}% of original list price, but contract time rose from {{ s.sfh.m.daysToContract.prior }} to {{ s.sfh.m.daysToContract.current }} days.

verdicts.label: Condos & townhomes
verdicts.note: Supply down from {{ s.condo.m.monthsSupply.prior | dec1 }} months but still elevated; contract time rose from {{ s.condo.m.daysToContract.prior }} to {{ s.condo.m.daysToContract.current }} days, on a small number of sales.

numbersLede: Every figure below is as reported for St. Lucie County. Percent change is year over year, {{ dataMonth }} versus {{ priorMonth }}.

insights.heading: What the Market Is Telling Us
insights.lede: What the {{ dataMonth }} figures point to, tied directly to the tables on page 3.

cards.title: Single-family sits close to balanced.
cards.body: Supply eased from {{ s.sfh.m.monthsSupply.prior | dec1 }} to {{ s.sfh.m.monthsSupply.current | dec1 }} months, and the typical sale closed at {{ s.sfh.m.olpReceived.current | dec1 }}% of original list price, up from {{ s.sfh.m.olpReceived.prior | dec1 }}%. Against that, median days to contract rose {{ s.sfh.m.daysToContract.pct | abspct }} to {{ s.sfh.m.daysToContract.current }}. Taken together the two sides roughly offset.

cards.title: The single-family median came in just below last year.
cards.body: The median sale price was {{ s.sfh.m.medianPrice.current | usd }}, compared with {{ s.sfh.m.medianPrice.prior | usd }} in {{ priorMonth }}, while closed sales slipped {{ s.sfh.m.closedSales.pct | abspct }} to {{ s.sfh.m.closedSales.current | int }}. A move of this size is within the range the county median has drifted across recent months and is not, on its own, evidence of a broad decline.

cards.title: There is less on the market than a year ago.
cards.body: Active single-family listings stood at {{ s.sfh.m.inventory.current | int }}, against {{ s.sfh.m.inventory.prior | int }} in {{ priorMonth }}. The decline is modest here compared with the counties to the south, which is part of why St. Lucie still reads as the most balanced of the three.

cards.title: Condos and townhomes remain buyer-leaning.
cards.body: Active inventory fell {{ s.condo.m.inventory.pct | abspct }} to {{ s.condo.m.inventory.current | int }} and supply dropped from {{ s.condo.m.monthsSupply.prior | dec1 }} months, yet {{ s.condo.m.monthsSupply.current | dec1 }} months still leaves buyers with options. Median days to contract lengthened to {{ s.condo.m.daysToContract.current }} from {{ s.condo.m.daysToContract.prior }}, so sellers should expect a longer marketing period.

cards.title: The condo median moves on very few sales.
cards.body: St. Lucie County is not a large condo market. The median was {{ s.condo.m.medianPrice.current | usd }} against {{ s.condo.m.medianPrice.prior | usd }} a year earlier, but it rests on {{ s.condo.m.closedSales.current | int }} closings, so which buildings happened to trade moves it more than any change in what units are worth. Read it alongside {{ s.condo.m.monthsSupply.current | dec1 }} months of supply, {{ s.condo.m.inventory.current | int }} active listings and {{ s.condo.m.olpReceived.current | dec1 }}% of original list price.

cards.title: Cash plays a very different role by property type.
cards.body: {{ cash.sfh }}% of single-family closings ({{ s.sfh.m.paidInCash.current | int }} of {{ s.sfh.m.closedSales.current | int }}) and {{ cash.condo }}% of condo/townhome closings ({{ s.condo.m.paidInCash.current | int }} of {{ s.condo.m.closedSales.current | int }}) were paid in cash, calculated from the reported counts.

insights.localLine: County figures blend varied local markets, such as Port St. Lucie, Fort Pierce, Tradition and Hutchinson Island, and conditions in any one of them can differ from the county median.

guidanceLede: The same county data calls for different moves depending on which side of the transaction you are on, and which property type you are dealing with.

disclaimer: These statistics describe past sales activity in St. Lucie County for the months shown.
